title: Iframes aren't reactivated when their page is restored from bfcache

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
When a traversal restores a bfcached top-level document, the documents of its child navigables aren't reactivated. [Get all navigables whose current session history entry will change or reload](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#get-all-navigables-whose-current-session-history-entry-will-change-or-reload) only checks a navigable's children when its own document doesn't change:

> If _targetEntry_'s document is _navigable_'s active document, and _targetEntry_'s document state's reload pending is false, then extend _navigablesToCheck_ with the child navigables of _navigable_.

The algorithm that gets navigables needing only a history length/index update has the same condition, and [reactivate a document](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/browsing-the-web.html#reactivate-a-document) doesn't recurse into descendants. So the iframes don't get `pageshow`, their `history.length`/index and `navigation.entries()` aren't updated, and no `dispose` fires for entries pruned while the page was in bfcache.

[`entries-after-bfcache-in-iframe.html`](https://wpt.fyi/results/navigation-api/navigation-history-entry/entries-after-bfcache-in-iframe.html) expects the iframe to get `pageshow` and `dispose` and its `entries()` to shrink. It passes in Chrome Canary and Safari TP, and fails in Firefox Nightly.

Maybe reactivating a document should also reactivate its descendants, each with its own entries for the navigation API.

(Found while looking into #13085.)
